**Thu 08.10.26, 16:15–17:45 · Room 4.B51** · Basic reading: KW ch. 6 (pp. 125–141); additional: KKV ch. 2, Gerring (2012), de Kadt & Grzymala-Busse (2025) · Applied reading: Barnes & Karim (2025), *The Manosphere and politics* · Presenters: **Rika Elena Hünerbach, Samantha Irving**

**Learning goals:** students can (1) classify variables as categorical, ordinal or continuous; (2) choose central tendency and spread measures by variable type and compute them in R; (3) read a histogram and a box plot; (4) name the criteria for good estimators; (5) derive descriptive questions from a theory.

**Before class:** presentation slides in OLAT (due Wed 07.10, 12:00)? · seminar question 5 uploaded? · grading sheet printed · deck rendered with the 2026 class list (`00_admin/classroom_2026.csv`) · deck in speaker view (press S)

**Checkpoints:** 16:35 start "Central tendency" · 16:55 start "Good descriptive inference" · **17:07 end share round** · **17:08 presentation starts** (25 min max., then discussion until 17:42) · **Content note** before the presentation: misogyny and violence against women

**Discussion prompts (if the room is quiet):** Snowball sampling from one starting list (SPLC): which population can the 140 sites describe? · What is left out (4chan, private channels, non-English sites)? · Intercoder agreement of 75.9% on subgroups: reliable enough (session 4)? · The typology is built from the same data it is meant to support: what would an independent test look like? · Which rung of the ladder does the paper reach?

**Grading (0–5 each, 15/30 = pass):** clarity · understanding · critique quality · reasoning · feasibility · discussion. Both presenters, one grade.
